variants.title: Lee and Charlton's disc: ebonite, steam heating
variants.note: Ebonite conducts about seven times worse than glass, so the disc is only 3 mm thick; disc B then settles near 84 °C.

source.title: Engineering ToolBox, thermal conductivity of common materials: rubber, hard (ebonite) about 0.16 W/(m K)

variants.title: Lee and Charlton's disc: glass, electrical heating
variants.note: An electrically heated block replaces the steam chest. The supply is set so the block settles at 85 °C, so the disc settles lower than with steam.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics: thermal conductivity of window (soda-lime) glass 1.05 W/(m K); brass specific heat 0.38 J/(g K)

variants.title: Lee and Charlton's disc: ebonite, electrical heating
variants.note: Electrical heating of the block, set to 85 °C, with the 3 mm ebonite disc.

source.title: Engineering ToolBox, thermal conductivity of common materials: rubber, hard (ebonite) about 0.16 W/(m K)
